newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA sees French car sales down in December.
newsitem.headline: PSA sees French car sales down in December.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet said on Wednesday that car orders had fallen since October, after the expiry at the end of September of a new-cars-for-old rebate scheme.
He told a news conference he expect a strong drop in car registrations in the fourth quarter after the sharp fall in November "and no doubt in December," he said.

Car registrations fell 21.7 percent in November after rising 24.7 percent in October and rocketing 85.7 percent in September. Overall, he said he expected a 10 percent rise in car sales in France in 1996 but a nine to 10 percent drop in 1997.

Calvet said the year-long two-tier rebate scheme accounted for between 225,000 and 250,000 registrations, benefitting the market around 25 percent more than a prior flat-rate scheme introduced by former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur.
He also said it skewed sales toward cheaper models but less than the prior scheme.

However, both schemes had the negative effects of creating sales peaks and troughs that made it harder to organise production and of distorting the notion of the price of a car in consumers' minds. price of a car. "The search for the best price has become the No. 1 criterion" for the car buyer, Calvet said.
He said he expected a flat European market of around 12.7 million cars in 1997.

He said his forecasts were based on the assumption that there would be no more government assistance programmes in France or elsewhere in Europe, such as Italy, where the possibility is being debated in the press.
